summary: onSave becomes async and writes the whole store to data/notes.json after each save. The router and HTTP server still treat its return value as a string.

findings.title: Async onSave breaks the synchronous dispatch caller
findings.problem: onSave now returns a Promise, and dispatch in src/router.js:7 passes that Promise back unchanged. The server in src/main.js:9 then calls res.end with that Promise instead of a string.
findings.consequence: Node's res.end throws a TypeError on a Promise argument, so every POST /save crashes the server process. The writeFile promise also floats, so a write failure becomes an unhandled rejection.
findings.fix: Make dispatch async and have the server await it before calling res.end. The server should catch errors and answer with a 500 status.

findings.title: New snapshot write has no covering test
findings.problem: onSave now writes the store to a file and returns a Promise. The repository has no test that covers this behaviour.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the save path, such as the broken caller, reach production without being caught.
findings.fix: Add a test that dispatches a save and checks both the response text and the snapshot file contents.
